solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Total chastity then for virgin?

definitions.meaning: complete chastity means having ... at all, read as two words ...
a virgin in the figurative sense is a beginner, someone untried in a field

explanation.surface: A wry question about whether perfect chastity is what makes someone a virgin.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as NO VICE and it describes total chastity; read whole it is a learner.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgin is used figuratively for someone inexperienced, a newcomer or beginner at something.

clue.text: A one-liner?

parts.note: a one-liner is usually a quick joke, but here it is taken literally as something running on a single line or rail

explanation.surface: A comedian's single quick joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway system with only a single track rail is literally a line made of one rail.

clue.text: Work of the features editor?

parts.note: a features editor works on a newspaper's feature articles; here the features are a face, edited by a surgeon

explanation.surface: What a newspaper's features editor does all day.
explanation.definitionFit: Facial features are reshaped by plastic surgeons doing appearance-improving operations, a literal editing of features.

clue.text: Drug dealer's bit of skirt is in court

indicators.note: in tells us that the pieces before it sit inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: a hem is the edging part of a skirt
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drug dealer's girlfriend has ended up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of skirt' looks like slang for a woman, but it is literally a part of a skirt. 'Drug dealer' sounds criminal but names a lawful seller of medicines.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist dispenses medicines, so is jokingly described as a legitimate seller of drugs.

clue.text: Quality of service addressed, as luck would have it

definitions.text: Quality of service addressed, as luck would have it

parts.words: Quality of service addressed, as luck would have it
parts.note: public service quality decided by where you live, that is your address, which is a matter of chance

explanation.surface: A complaint that standards of public service depend on luck.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the phrase describes health or council services varying by area, so treatment depends on the code of your address.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the British idiom for public services varying by area, so your address decides what you receive.

clue.text: Risk inhaling dope as a dog

indicators.note: inhaling means taking something inside, so the word for dope goes inside the word for risk

parts.note: to risk money is to bet it
a dope is a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: A warning about the danger of breathing in drugs, with a dog for comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-legged long-eared hound bred for hunting by scent is one breed of dog.

clue.text: Shah Jahan's home town in Margate? On the contrary

indicators.note: on the contrary tells us to read the found letters the other way round
in signals that the letters are found inside the word Margate

explanation.surface: Asks whether a Mughal emperor came from Margate, an English seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' reverses ARGA, found inside Margate. Margate is an English seaside resort in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan ruled from this Indian city, where he built the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: Engine getting round the bend

definitions.meaning: a railway engine, a locomotive, shortened
round the bend is slang for crazy, mad

explanation.surface: A train engine going round a curve in the track.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway locomotive is shortened in casual use, and the same word is Spanish-derived slang for mad.

clue.text: Bear with shaved head? Well I never!

indicators.note: with its head shaved off, the first letter is removed

parts.note: Pooh is the bear in A. A. Milne's stories

explanation.surface: A bear with a shaved head surprises an onlooker.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise or amazement.

clue.text: Fruit, a round variety

parts.note: a round shape is a ring, the letter O
a range is a variety or assortment

explanation.surface: A fruit described as a round kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A round citrus fruit is one example of a fruit.

clue.text: Wind is back with low murmur, initially

indicators.note: back means the word is is read backwards

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of murmur

explanation.surface: A wind returns with a soft low murmur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective describing the murmur, but it is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot, dry, dust-laden desert wind of Arabia and North Africa.

clue.text: Bird wasn't 16 — cuckoo!

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the answer to 16 down, a flightless bird

explanation.surface: Someone insists the bird wasn't 16 down, it was a cuckoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' poses as another bird but is the anagram signal for WASNT plus EMU, the answer to 16.
explanation.definitionFit: A common white swan of Europe is one kind of bird.

clue.text: Spot the ball competition

parts.note: spot the ball is a newspaper game of guessing the hidden ball; here the ball is placed on the penalty spot in a football contest

explanation.surface: A newspaper game where you guess where the ball was in a photo.
explanation.walkthrough: Spot the Ball is a British newspaper competition; here 'spot' is the penalty spot in football.
explanation.definitionFit: A football tiebreak in which kicks are taken from the penalty spot is a competition with the ball spotted.

clue.text: I'm disgusted with leaders in union getting huffy

indicators.note: leaders in means the first letters of the next three words

explanation.surface: Someone disgusted that union leaders are getting huffy.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation used to express disgust or horror.

clue.text: Long-necked creature among sheep, some horse!

indicators.note: among means the creature goes inside the word for a group of sheep

parts.note: a flock is a group of sheep
E.T., the film alien, has a long extending neck

explanation.surface: A giraffe-like animal among sheep, and an impressive horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some horse!' looks like admiration, but means a part of a horse. 'Long-necked creature' suggests a giraffe; it is E.T.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint on a horse's leg just above the hoof is a part of the animal.

clue.text: Flightless bird I'm not sure should take drug to get high?

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting high means the letters climb upwards, read backwards

parts.note: um is a hesitant noise of uncertainty
E is short for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: An uncertain question whether a flightless bird should take drugs to get high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To get high' sounds like drug use, but in a down clue it reverses UME upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The large Australian bird that cannot fly.

clue.text: Loaded pistol finally getting in the way, having gone off

indicators.note: getting in means the last letter of pistol goes inside the other letters
gone off means gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged
finally means take the last letter of pistol

explanation.surface: A loaded pistol gets in the way and goes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having gone off' rearranges THE WAY into WEATHY, and 'getting in' puts L inside it. 'Loaded' looks like the pistol's state, but means rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is slang for rich, having plenty of money.

clue.text: Poetry in a heap of fruit?

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit
a rick is a heap or stack of hay

explanation.surface: Asks whether there is poetry in a pile of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads 'a heap of fruit' as fruit heap, LIME then RICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-line comic verse form is one kind of poetry.

clue.text: First of novels penned by horror writer, an impressive thing

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed in, so the letter goes inside the writer's name

parts.note: Bram Stoker wrote Dracula

indicators.note: first of means take the opening letter of novels

explanation.surface: The first of a horror writer's novels is a remarkable work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned by' suggests writing, but here means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for something striking or outstanding.

clue.text: Terribly traumatic on getting into aggressive music for a period in New York, perhaps?

definitions.text: a period in New York, perhaps?

indicators.note: getting into means the rearranged letters go inside the word for the music

parts.note: punk is loud aggressive rock music

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A traumatic spell spent in New York's punk scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges TRAUMATIC ON into CTUATIONMAR. Americans call the full stop a period, so a period in New York is a typographical mark.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage the full stop is called a period, an example of a symbol used in writing.

clue.text: Weep, hugging tree, struggling to speak

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping round, so the tree goes inside the word for weep

parts.note: to weep is to cry
an oak is a tree

explanation.surface: A tearful tree-hugger too choked up to talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoarse in voice, finding it hard to talk clearly.

clue.text: 'Are you sure?' 'Very much!'

definitions.meaning: a reply expressing doubt or surprise, asking for confirmation
used as an emphatic adverb meaning truly or very

explanation.surface: A brief exchange: one asks for certainty, the other insists strongly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works both as a doubting interjection and as an intensifying adverb.

clue.text: To swamp horse returns, providing transport in winter

parts.note: a bog is a swamp

indicators.note: returns means the word for horse is read backwards

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A horse comes back to a swamp, offering winter transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A long sled used for sliding down snowy slopes is a means of transport in winter.

clue.text: Master breaking leg in country

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open, so the master's letters go inside

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A master breaks his leg abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also the on side, so leg gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultanate on the Arabian Peninsula is a country.

clue.text: Comic-book hero knocking over short fascist vermin

indicators.note: knocking over turns the pieces upside down, so they read backwards
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a Nazi is a fascist
a rat is vermin

explanation.surface: A comic-book hero knocks down a fascist and some vermin.
explanation.definitionFit: The jungle hero raised by apes, created by Edgar Rice Burroughs, starred in comic books.

clue.text: Angel cake maker scoffing cake's topping

indicators.note: scoffing means eating, so the letter goes inside the cake maker

parts.note: a baker makes cakes

indicators.note: topping means the top, first letter of cake's

explanation.surface: A cake maker eats the icing off a cake, called an angel cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angel cake' looks like one item; 'Angel' is the definition, a theatrical financier.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a person who finances a theatrical show, a supporter or sponsor.

clue.text: Go off royal couple?

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
R for Rex, the king, pairs with the queen to make a couple

explanation.surface: Asks whether a royal couple have gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the Queen's cipher; R for Rex completes the royal couple.
explanation.definitionFit: To go off is to go wrong or stray, as to make a mistake.

clue.text: Little beast showing bit of leg

definitions.meaning: a young cow or other young animal
the fleshy back of the lower leg

explanation.surface: A small animal showing some leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a young bovine animal and the muscle at the back of the shin.
